In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the activity of neurons in the hypothalamic PVN that synthesize and secrete the antidiuretic hormone vasopressin.
the role of the subfornial organ (SFO), a circumventricular organ, in regulating the activity and secretion of vasopressin from the hypothalamo-neurohypophysial system.

the role of the subfornicula organ (SFO), the anterior hypothalamus (AHA), and the median preoptic area (MnPO), in the regulation of the activity of vasopressin-secreting neurons in hypothalamic parvocellular neurosecretory neurons (pPVN).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SFO is a major brain site of action of circulating ANG II in the control of the activity of VP-secreting neurons in rats.

circulating ANG-II excites SFO neurons, which then excites MnPO neurons and that the latter release ANG-II as an excitatory neurotransmitter to the PVN to cause enhanced activity of putatitive VP-secreting neurons.

the SFO-MnPO-PVN circuit is involved in the central control of the activity of VP-secreting neurons in response to circulating ANG II.
